questions.question: How does framing influence the way people understand news? / [CO2, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• How does framing influence the way people understand news?
  • • Framing refers to the way news stories are presented — the angle, language, and emphasis chosen — which
  • shapes how audiences interpret and assign meaning to events
  • • The same event framed differently can evoke contrasting emotional responses and political conclusions in
  • audiences
  • • Framing influences public opinion by highlighting certain aspects of an issue while downplaying others,
  • reflecting the editorial or ideological priorities of the media outlet

questions.question: Discuss the importance of credibility and respect for others in citizen journalism. / [CO2, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the importance of credibility and respect for others in citizen journalism
  • • Credibility is the cornerstone of citizen journalism — without verified, accurate, and fairly presented
  • information, citizen reports risk causing harm and losing public trust
  • • Building credibility requires transparent sourcing, corroboration of facts from multiple sources, clear
  • distinction between fact and opinion, and willingness to issue corrections
  • • Respect for others demands that citizen journalists protect the dignity, privacy, and safety of individuals
  • featured in their reports, particularly vulnerable subjects
  • • Avoiding sensationalism, stereotyping, and intrusive reporting upholds the ethical standard that journalism
  • — professional or citizen — must not cause unnecessary harm
  • • When citizen journalism demonstrates consistent credibility and respectful practice, it earns legitimacy
  • alongside professional media and strengthens the democratic information ecosystem

questions.question: Explain objectivity, clarity, and fact-based communication in citizen journalism. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain objectivity, clarity, and fact-based communication in citizen journalism
  • • Objectivity requires citizen journalists to present multiple perspectives fairly, minimise personal bias, and
  • distinguish between factual reporting and personal opinion
  • • While complete objectivity is debated in media theory, striving for impartiality ensures that citizen journalism
  • informs rather than manipulates audiences
  • • Clarity demands that reports are written or presented in accessible, unambiguous language — avoiding
  • jargon, complex sentence structures, and assumptions about audience knowledge
  • • Fact-based communication requires verification of all claims through credible sources, official records,
  • eyewitness accounts, or documented evidence before publication
  • • Together, these principles elevate citizen journalism from personal commentary to a legitimate, trustworthy
  • form of public information that complements professional media practice

questions.question: Elaborate on the essential tools and techniques a citizen journalist requires to practise journalism effectively? / [CO3] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate on the essential tools and techniques a citizen journalist requires to practise journalism effectively?
  • • Hardware tools — a smartphone with a quality camera, external microphone, portable tripod, power bank,
  • and mobile data connectivity form the basic citizen journalist's kit
  • • Recording and production tools — video recording apps, mobile audio recorders, and editing apps such as
  • CapCut, GarageBand, and Adobe Rush enable field production and post-production without professional
  • equipment
  • • Publishing platforms — blogs (WordPress), social media (YouTube, Instagram, Twitter/X), and community
  • news platforms serve as distribution channels for citizen journalism content
  • • Verification tools — Google Reverse Image Search, InVID, Snopes, and fact-checking databases help citizen
  • journalists verify information and images before publishing
  • • Ethical and legal awareness — understanding defamation law, privacy rights, informed consent, and
  • copyright is as essential as any technical tool in ensuring responsible, sustainable citizen journalism practice
